holding_summary: The court held that a parol agreement by which Shamburg would occupy several rooms in the leased farmhouse and be boarded there by the lessee's wife was a valid collateral contract, not barred as evidence varying the written farm lease. It further held it was error to instruct the jury that the rental value of the rooms could be deducted from Shamburg's claim merely because he continued occupying them after a notice to vacate, since continued boarding and occupancy without any change of terms works no forfeiture or added charge against the boarder.

quotes.text: Notice to a boarder and occupant of a room to quit, followed by no other action than a continuance of boarding and occupancy as before the notice, makes no change in the contract as regards compensation.
Had Beaver ceased to board Shamburg and his family, the case would be different. Telling him to go, and afterwards inducing him to stay, leaves the case as if Beaver had said nothing.

We think it was error to instruct the jury that the .plaintiff “is entitled to have deducted, by way of equitable defense, the rental value of four rooms which he alleges that Dr. Shamburg persisted in occupying after notice to vacate the same,” and the first assignment of error must be sustained.
